Operator directive: pass this along as a candidate for a bend2 law. Found and fixed just now, filed as https://github.com/Flip-Engineering/baton/issues/556 (bug, priority:high, not a law proposal itself -- that's your call to make).

The failure: a resident's git `origin` was configured to a local filesystem checkout instead of the canonical shared remote (GitHub). A `git push` from that resident reported success. A `git fetch` + `git log origin/<branch>` from the SAME resident confirmed the push, showing the commit present. Every verification available from inside that resident said the publish had landed correctly. It hadn't -- the commit only reached the local intermediate checkout. This was only caught because the operator asked a suspicious staleness question that prompted a cross-check from a completely separate checkout's own real origin.

Operator's framing: this should not be allowed or possible in Baton -- a write that reports success must actually have reached the canonical destination, or the report must say otherwise. This looks squarely relevant to your M-3 (publication eligibility/evidence conditions) and M-11 (no fabrication of established execution/verification/publication facts) from the laws-proposed set, but I'm not asserting it fits cleanly into either as-is or needs its own entry -- that's exactly the kind of scope judgment you've been getting right throughout this review, so bringing you the concrete case rather than a pre-formed proposal.

If that's cleanly stateable and checkable as its own law given what you now know about Bend2's actual proof shapes, say so plainly and propose it as its own entry. If you think it's better absorbed into an existing clause, say which one and why the absorbed version still bans the exact case described (a resident's origin silently misconfigured to a local path, with push/fetch/log all appearing to succeed) -- not a weaker, general "be truthful about publication" statement that this case could still slip past.
